briefing:
The Stockholm Conference has opened successfully with 40 delegations and produced a remarkable first-day breakthrough: Russia's formal tabling of a revised M2 proposal accepting the US nuclear storage site verification formula, coupled with a 96-hour synchronized implementation window for all three M2 elements (Iskander satellite verification, reciprocal NATO base transparency limited to nuclear-capable storage sites, and synchronized ELEVATED-to-PEACETIME nuclear de-escalation). The five principals (US, Russia, UK, France, Turkey) have a draft M2 Implementation Protocol circulating, with the Czech Verification Working Group assigned to refine technical details on Day 2.

The military situation continues its steady transition to permanent deterrence architecture. Poland's IRIS-T SLM joint C2 systems interface document has been formally signed with Germany, advancing the binational corridor air defense toward operational integration. The US Phase 1 drawdown has reached 85%, and NATO permanent basing construction at Rukla, Tapa, and Camp Adazi all advance ahead of schedule. The corridor transit regime has processed 144 cumulative transits with zero violations, and Grodno-Kybartai civilian crossings continue above 1,000 daily under full OSCE monitoring.

The principal diplomatic challenge shifts from whether an M2 agreement is possible to the technical details of implementation. The 96-hour window, SIPRI intermediary role, Chang Guang satellite cadence, and CEP enforcement triggers must all be codified in language acceptable to all parties. Lithuania's insistence on suspension rights and snap-back provisions remains the most sensitive element for Russia, while Moscow's demand for true reciprocity in satellite verification of NATO nuclear-capable storage sites tests alliance transparency norms. China's deepening economic stake -- now approximately $9B conditional on M2 -- creates powerful momentum but also raises questions about Beijing's growing influence in European security architecture.

Public opinion across NATO remains firmly in the de-escalation corridor, with war support below 30% in most Western capitals and government approval benefiting from visible diplomatic progress. The economic environment is benign: oil at $83.50, gas prices easing, and Baltic shipping at 95% of pre-crisis levels. Markets are pricing in Stockholm success, meaning any collapse in negotiations would trigger a sharp reversal. All parties enter Day 2 understanding that the Verification Working Group's technical refinement of the M2 Implementation Protocol is the most consequential arms control drafting exercise since the INF Treaty.
narrative:
Day 21 of the Suwalki Gap crisis marked a historic turning point as the Stockholm Conference on European Security Architecture opened at the Waterfront Congress Centre with 40 delegations -- the most consequential multilateral European security negotiation since the Helsinki Final Act of 1975. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson welcomed delegates with an address emphasizing that 'the architecture we build here must outlast the crisis that brought us together,' setting a tone of institutional ambition that resonated throughout the opening plenary.

The opening day was dominated by a carefully choreographed diplomatic sequence. In the morning plenary, Lithuania delivered a powerful frontline state statement, with Foreign Minister Gabrielius Landsbergis declaring that suspension rights and automatic snap-back provisions were 'non-negotiable elements of Baltic sovereignty' -- drawing sustained applause from the Eastern European delegations. The Czech Republic then presented the Enhanced Verification Ladder as the procedural foundation, distributing the final three-tier framework document to all 40 delegations and confirming Day 2's Verification Working Group agenda. Russia's Deputy Foreign Minister Grushko, operating under expanded Kremlin authority, delivered a measured opening statement signaling Moscow's readiness to engage constructively on the M2 pathway, specifically referencing the 'nuclear storage site reciprocal verification formula' as a basis for discussion -- the first public Russian acknowledgment of convergence with the US position.

The critical diplomatic breakthrough came in the afternoon margins. Turkey's Foreign Minister Fidan hosted an informal trilateral corridor conversation between Grushko and the UK-France co-guarantor principals, in which Russia formally tabled a revised M2 proposal: acceptance of the US nuclear storage site formula for reciprocal satellite imagery (dropping the demand for full Ramstein/Incirlik transparency), coupled with a request for a 96-hour synchronized implementation window (extended from the original 72-hour demand). The UK and France communicated this immediately to Washington, where NSC Director Kellogg authorized acceptance of the 96-hour window as consistent with US instructions, provided SIPRI serves as the neutral verification intermediary. By evening, a draft M2 Implementation Protocol was circulating among the five principals (US, Russia, UK, France, Turkey) with the Czech Verification Working Group assigned to refine technical details on Day 2.

Military developments continued their steady transition from crisis to permanent architecture. Poland's TARCZA POKOJU Phase 2 entered Day 12 with the seventh battalion beginning familiarization, while the IRIS-T SLM joint command-and-control architecture with Germany reached its first technical milestone: the systems interface document was formally signed by Polish and German defense officials in a Stockholm side meeting. Germany's Zeitenwende East program at Rukla advanced to 58% structural steel completion, and the DICE-EF second tranche disbursement planning began. The US completed its Phase 1 drawdown to 85%, with the forward Augustow presence reduced to approximately 150 support personnel. Canada's Camp Adazi permanent construction reached a new milestone with the vehicle maintenance facility achieving weather-tight status. Belarus completed its fourth prisoner transfer, delivering two political prisoners to Lithuanian custody under OSCE escort. China's PBoC representative held bilateral meetings with both Russian and European delegations, confirming the full $9B conditional package and offering expanded Chang Guang satellite verification cadence -- monthly instead of quarterly for the first 12 months.
